reclassification_49.note: Supersedes the predecessor task's flat 'Category 4 (Main Domain & Cross-Domain Utilities / Promotion Review / PM12 League)' label (which was a single boilerplate bucket) with three semantically distinct groups, consistent with REBASELINE Appendix B's instruction that cross-domain shared tools must not be folded into a single domain owner.

group_A_promotion_review_human_inbox_pm1.description: A cohesive Promotion Review / Human Inbox / PM12 League bounded context. These functions call each other extensively (e.g. _human_inbox_decision_projection_from_record -> _human_inbox_decision_recommendation_id -> _promotion_review_clean_id / _promotion_review_target_id / _promotion_review_revision_recommendation_id / _promotion_review_revision_id). This is governance/human-gate domain logic, not persona domain and not a generic utility; it does not fit personas/service.py or auth/policy.py.
group_A_promotion_review_human_inbox_pm1.proposed_owner: new module, e.g. services/control-plane/bff/promotion_review/service.py (directory does not yet exist; services/control-plane/bff/governance/service.py and services/control-plane/bff/command_adapters/service.py are existing sibling domain-service modules with the same shape and are the closest precedent for the target module layout)

group_B_persona_fleet_projection.description: Conceptually persona domain (fleet health/lifecycle projection), but the predecessor task deliberately kept these in main.py because personas/service.py already holds an independently-evolved second implementation under the same name with a real behavioral or signature difference (documented in predecessor evidence.json divergent_adjudication_19). Folding these requires per-function adjudication of which body is canonical, not a blind move.
group_B_persona_fleet_projection.proposed_owner: services/control-plane/bff/personas/service.py (already a declared artifact of this task -- no contract revision needed for this group, but the merge itself is nontrivial and out of scope for this delivery)

group_C_generic_cross_domain_utility.description: Stateless, side-effect-free helpers (float coercion, nested-dict lookup, record sorting/merging, generic param resolution) with no domain semantics. These are the closest fit to REBASELINE Appendix B's '通用工具/型別轉換/聚合' buckets and must not be folded into either persona or promotion-review domain modules.

deferred_members.name: _project_final_command_response
deferred_members.reason: Body (identical in both main.py and personas/service.py) calls three helpers -- _action_command_status_from_command_status, _project_command_submission_response, _command_dual_write_receipts -- that are defined only in main.py and are not part of the Group C scope. personas/service.py's own copy calls these same three names but never imports or defines them: this is a pre-existing latent defect (NameError at runtime if personas/service.py's copy is actually invoked, e.g. at personas/service.py:1037) that predates this task. Moving this function into the shared module without first resolving that dependency would require pulling in the three helpers too, which are cross-domain-scoped to Group A's promotion-review/command bounded context, not Group C's generic-utility scope. Left both copies in place unchanged; the pre-existing NameError defect is flagged for a separate follow-up, not fixed by this task.

verification_performed.byte_level_identity_check: AST-extracted each of the 10 Group C function bodies (source text including decorators) from both main.py and personas/service.py and diffed them; 9 of 10 were byte-identical, 1 (_ppl_alloc_009_paper_environment_guard) differed only in an import-alias style (main.py: auth_policy.bool_from_env(...); personas/service.py: bool_from_env(...)) both resolving to the same canonical services/control-plane/bff/auth/policy.py:bool_from_env, confirmed not a behavioral divergence. Re-diffed the new shared-module copies against the original main.py bodies after writing them to confirm exact match (module-alias substitution excepted).
verification_performed.dependency_check: For each of the 10 members, checked whether the function body calls any name not itself in Group C; found _project_final_command_response depends on three main.py-only helpers outside Group C scope (see group_C_generic_cross_domain_utility.deferred_members above) and left it in place; the other 9 have no such external dependency beyond auth/policy.py (already canonical) and stdlib/typing/fastapi.
verification_performed.ast_isolation_test_dependency: test_pathreon_market_persona_fleet_contract.py, tests/test_bff_persona_provisioning_baseline_500.py, tests/test_bff_pm12_persona_league.py, management_read_models/test_persona_fleet_read_failures.py, and tests/test_mgmt_read_001_persona_fleet_owner_observations.py all ast.parse() main.py directly and re-exec extracted top-level ast.FunctionDef nodes by name for isolated testing without importing the full FastAPI app graph. Updated each to inject the migrated functions (imported from services.control_plane.bff.shared.cross_domain_utils) into the exec namespace instead of relying on the now-deleted main.py source nodes.

Did not have budget for a byte-for-byte baseline diff of the full 4000+ test suite; the targeted verification above is the primary regression evidence for this change.
